title: Throughput Proof Suite: orchestrator, workload-replay simulator, and customer pilot checklist
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Build a reusable "Throughput Proof Suite (TPS)" that certifies Dedicated capacity commitments for customers. The suite will provide a reproducible benchmarking methodology, a workload-replay / synthetic-workload simulator, an orchestrator for distributed agents that run tests across a fleet, and a customer-facing signoff checklist/report.

Goals:
- Produce deterministic throughput attestations customers can rely on for SLA contracts (throughput and tail latency).
- Provide repeatable test scenarios that exercise autoscaling policies, burst handling, and degradation/fallback behavior.
- Generate artifacts for legal/purchase reviews: signed report, raw telemetry, and a minimal replay bundle customers can run in their environment.

Scope of first iteration (MVP):
1) Workload-replay simulator that can: ingest anonymized customer traces or synthesize representative mixes (chat vs. embedding vs. long-context generations), apply sequence-length distributions, and emit requests with configurable arrival processes (Poisson, Pareto bursts, deterministic ramps).
2) Orchestrator to schedule runs across Dedicated pools, collect Prometheus metrics, request-level traces (trace id, kernel selection), and token-level error counts.
3) Benchmark protocol: ramp (10m), warmup (5m), steady-state (30m), burst injection (3 x microbursts), cooldown (5m). Capture p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9 latency, qps, tokens/sec, error rate, and autoscaler reaction time.
4) Acceptance criteria template for customers: throughput >= committed RU (tokens/sec) at p95 latency <= 200ms for short generations, p99 < 500ms, error rate < 0.1% over steady-state window, autoscaler scales to required nodes within policy window (configurable by customer).
5) Report generator that exports PDF summary, CSV of raw samples, and a JSON attestation bundle containing test metadata and signature.

Benchmarking methodology details:
- Workload composition: support a taxonomy of request archetypes (SmallChat, MediumChat, LongForm, Embedding-S, Embedding-L). Each archetype has sequence-length and compute cost distributions derived from production telemetry sampling (sanitized).
- KV cache warmup: before steady-state measurement, run a warmed cache phase (configurable) and measure delta between cold and warm throughputs. Document recommended warming strategy for customers.
- Batching profiles: run sweeps over batch_size and target_latency to produce a Pareto frontier for cost vs latency. Store recommended batch profiles per model + instance type.
- Failure injection: network glitches, synthetic OOM on a worker, and model fallback path. Confirm graceful degradation and correct routing to fallback variants when capacity constrained.
- Autoscaler observability: measure time from sustained queue depth to scale-up action, node readiness time, and the resulting throughput delta.

Operational implementation notes:
- Agents run small Python harness that uses Redwood SDK to replay requests and publish metrics to Prometheus pushed gateway when necessary. Orchestrator is a lightweight controller (k8s Job-based for Hosted, internal scheduler for Dedicated).
- Use a reproducible seed for synthetic workloads and keep a versioned corpus in: https://drive.redwood.ai/bench/corpora.
- Store run artifacts in a dedicated S3 bucket with retention 90 days, link to customer portal for downloads.

Acceptance test checklist (customer-facing):
- Test metadata: model, instance type, runtime-1.24 commit, region, pool-id.
- Run ID and reproducible command to rerun.
- Key metrics: certified tokens/sec, p99 latency, error rate, autoscaler reaction quantiles.
- Signed attestation JSON + link to raw telemetry.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Replaying customer traces can leak PII if not sanitized correctly; use existing telemetry scrubbing pipeline and add a mandatory review step.
- Deterministic load replay across heterogeneous fleets is difficult; we must version agent harness and include host/driver metadata so results can be normalized.
- Measurement noise: need multiple runs and statistical aggregation to avoid single-run anomalies influencing certification.

MVP Deliverables:
- TPS orchestrator service (v0.1) + agent harness
- Benchmark protocol doc and runbook (confluence)
- Customer signoff template and attestation generator
- Example run against a dedicated demo pool and initial report

Longer-term enhancements (post-MVP): tenant-aware stress profiles, automated canary gating for rollouts, integration into Console for self-serve certification, and legal-grade signing using KMS/HSM.
